key_insight: A recursive deep learning pipeline can replace slow finite-element simulations to predict the full transverse-compression response of synthetic plant fibers and their effective modulus.
engineering_relevance: This enables high-throughput mechanical screening of realistic natural-fiber geometries, supporting faster design of sustainable fiber-reinforced composites.
method: Two coupled recursive U-Nets predict step-by-step deformation and internal stress evolution under transverse compression.
A regression CNN uses the final stress field to estimate transverse Young’s modulus.
Trained on 1,000 synthetic hemp-like cross-sections with FE ground truth, including cases with and without lumen.
evidence_signal: The model achieved SSIM 0.9574 ± 0.0074 and RMSE 0.0345 ± 0.0079 for stress-field sequences, and predicted modulus with R² = 0.938 ± 0.024, MAE = 24.31 ± 1.23 MPa, and MAPE = 5.25 ± 0.91%, while inference took under one second versus about five minutes for FE.
watch_item: Performance is demonstrated on synthetic fibers derived from real cross-sections, so generalization to unseen species, broader defect patterns, or experimental measurements still needs validation.
paper_title: Deep Learning-based Mechanical Characterization of Synthetically Generated Plant Fibers under Transverse Compression
